SSD наконец-то могут подешеветь — цены на память NAND пошли вниз⁠. Цены на чипы NAND за месяц упали на 20%.

После продолжительного роста цены на флеш-память NAND начали снижаться. По данным Seoul Economic Daily, за последний месяц спотовые цены упали примерно на 20%. Отдельные категории подешевели ещё сильнее: например, стоимость 512-гигабитных чипов снизилась на 32% по сравнению с предыдущим кварталом. В то же время стоимость терабитных чипов снизилась на 19%.

Одной из главных причин стало ослабление потребительского спроса. Из-за подорожания памяти SSD, оперативной памяти, смартфоны и компьютеры стали слишком дорогими для многих покупателей. Пользователи откладывают обновление техники, а производители сокращают объёмы накопителей в устройствах, чтобы удерживать цены на приемлемом уровне.

Аналитики Bank of America ожидают, что контрактные цены на потребительскую NAND-память в первом квартале 2027 года снизятся ещё на 5–10%. В перспективе это может привести к удешевлению SSD, ноутбуков и смартфонов. Однако розничные цены не обязательно изменятся сразу: производителям и продавцам сначала предстоит распродать запасы компонентов, закупленных по прежним расценкам.

В целом рынок NAND может перейти к избытку предложения уже в 2027 году. Это создаёт предпосылки для дальнейшего снижения стоимости потребительских SSD.

JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America announced similar policies last month, while PNC Bank adjusted its terms on November 18. Citizens Bank also sent emails to customers this week, reminding them that they are responsible for actions performed by AI assistants. The Citibank agreement further states that customers using AI agents provided by Citibank do not incur additional liability.

🇰🇿 Аэропорт Алматы увеличил пропускную способность терминала внутренних рейсов почти втрое

В Международном аэропорту Алматы завершили модернизацию терминала внутренних рейсов Т1, сообщили в Минтрансе.

Инвестиции в реконструкцию составили около $32 млн.

После обновления терминал сможет обслуживать до 9 млн пассажиров в год.

↗️ Это на 5,8 млн человек или в 2,8 раза больше, чем до модернизации.

В ходе реконструкции:
• обновили зону регистрации площадью 1 700 м² и установили 23 стойки;
• расширили проход предполётного досмотра с 2 до 3,5 м;
• увеличили число автоматических турникетов с трёх до пяти;
• установили три новых телетрапа;
• увеличили протяжённость багажных конвейеров с 85 до 228 м.

ℹ Реконструкция началась в сентябре 2025 года в рамках программы Horizon — первого этапа мастер-плана развития аэропорта до 2050 года.

„Technische Störungen“ scheinen jetzt FAST TÄGLICH zu passieren.

Добрый день, друзья! ☀ Краткие новости 🗞 в мире криптовалют на сегодня от Сrypto Сyber Future! 

Сегодня, 19 ноября, крипторынок по-прежнему в «красной зоне», а главные новости — про ставку ФРС, расчистку последствий взлома Binance и старт криптоторгов в России. Вот что происходит.

Рынок: биткоин у четырёхмесячных минимумов
Биткоин утром торговался около $63,5 тыс., внутри дня опускался до $62,4 тыс. — самого низкого уровня с июля. За неделю он потерял около 13–14%. 

Главная причина давления — ожидания повышения ставки ФРС в декабре: протокол октябрьского заседания показал, что всё больше членов комитета за ужесточение политики, некоторые — за шаг сразу на 50 базисных пунктов. Дополнительный отток средств спровоцировало IPO Anthropic на Nasdaq, которое состоялось сегодня. 
Из американских биткоин-ETF с начала ноября вывели уже $2,34 млрд, а предложение стейблкоинов за месяц сократилось на $14–16 млрд — свободных денег на рынке становится меньше. BlackRock возобновила оттоки из IBIT после однодневной паузы. 

Индекс страха и жадности рухнул до 10 пунктов — зона крайнего страха. За сутки ликвидированы позиции 92,5 тыс. трейдеров на $408 млн, основной удар пришёлся на лонги. Аналитики спорят: ключевой тест — поддержка $60 тыс.; если её пробьют, рынок может искать дно в диапазоне $55–58 тыс. 

На этом фоне инвестбанки парадоксально наращивают позиции: Goldman Sachs за квартал удвоил пакет в биткоин-ETF до $1,28 млрд, Wells Fargo и Bank of America также увеличили вложения. 

Регулирование и Россия
СПБ Биржа запустила тестовые торги биткоином, Ethereum и USDT и направила в ЦБ документы для старта реальных торгов. Российские биржи получат право торговать криптовалютами с 22 ноября, Мосбиржа планирует пилотный запуск с 1 декабря. 

ЦБ готовит обязательное тестирование инвесторов как условие доступа к крипторынку — систему планируют запустить до 1 декабря. Неквалифицированные инвесторы смогут покупать активы с лимитом 300 тыс. рублей в год через одного посредника. 

Минфин начал разработку правил бухучета криптовалют — тема войдёт в ежегодные рекомендации аудиторам, детальных требований пока не будет, обозначат общие риски. 

Безопасность и скандалы

Скандал со вскрытыми кошельками Ledger дошёл до Берлина и Дубая: в устройства встраивали компоненты, перехватывающие сид-фразу при первой настройке. Двое покупателей в Дубае потеряли суммарно $604 тыс. Ledger просит всех, кто покупал кошельки в Берлине с января 2026 года, обратиться в поддержку; уязвимостей в чипе и прошивке не нашли, устройства можно бесплатно проверить в том числе на рентгене на заводе во Франции. 
Суд в Абу-Даби сохранил заморозку активов на $2,85 млрд из украденных при взломе Binance 29 октября (общая сумма кражи — около $6,3 млрд; биржа назвала это крупнейшим взломом в истории криптоиндустрии). В распоряжении фигурируют 18 компаний, включая Circle и World Liberty Financial. 

Компаниям и фондам

Майнеры переквалифицируются в ИИ-компании: MARA с сентября продала 13 597 BTC и направляет деньги в инфраструктуру для ИИ, Riot Platforms за 9 месяцев реализовала 20 264 BTC и заключила соглашение о размещении мощностей для Anthropic. 
Strategy (крупнейший держатель биткоина) покупает всё меньше монет: на прошлой неделе всего 485 BTC на $33 млн, при этом на выкуп своих облигаций STRC потратила $228 млн. Её бумажный убыток по запасу в 850 тыс. BTC — около $9,6 млрд, а 30 ноября компанию исключат из индексов MSCI. 

HSBC разрешил клиентам покупать токенизированные акции фонда через собственный стейблкоин RedCoin (RCHKD) — расчёты идут через блокчейн в соотношении 1:1 к гонконгскому доллару. 
Bitwise готовит спотовый ETF на Zcash, а администрация США запустила Центр пресечения угроз для перекрытия криптодоходов мошенников — партнёром стала аналитическая компания TRM Labs. 

Главная интрига ближайших дней — протокол заседания ФРС и реакция рынка на уровень $60 тыс.

소비자용 낸드 현물가 한 달 새 20% 하락… SSD·노트북·스마트폰 가격도 내려갈까
뱅크오브아메리카(BofA)는 2027년 1분기 PC·스마트폰용 낸드플래시 고정거래가격이 5~10% 하락할 것으로 전망했다. 스마트폰과 PC 수요가 줄어든 가운데 중국 업체의 공급까지 늘면서 소비자용 낸드 시장에 공급 과잉 압력이 커지고 있다.

지난 2년 사이 SSD와 스마트폰, 노트북, 태블릿 가격이 일제히 크게 올랐다. PC를 조립하거나 전자기기를 구매하려는 소비자에게는 치솟은 DDR5 메모리 가격만 부담이었던 게 아니다. AI 붐의 여파로 SSD도 용량을 가리지 않고 비싸졌다. 그런데 최근 소비자용 낸드플래시 현물가격이 하락하면서 이런 흐름이 바뀔 조짐이 나타났다고 서울경제가 보도했다.

서울경제에 따르면 낸드 현물가격은 최근 한 달 사이 20% 하락했다. 뱅크오브아메리카가 11월 13일 자 보고서에서 전한 업계 분위기도 이와 비슷하다. 은행이 접촉한 업계 관계자들은 낸드 가격이 조정 국면에 접어들 것으로 내다봤다.

서울경제가 인용한 보고서에 따르면, 웨이퍼 상태로 거래되는 512Gb(기가비트) 낸드의 현물가격은 32% 하락한 14.30달러, 1Tb(테라비트) 제품은 19% 하락한 24.90달러였다. 또 다른 업계 관계자는 서울경제에 “낸드 가격이 지금까지와 같은 가파른 상승세를 이어가기는 어렵다”고 말했다.

기업용 SSD 가격이 연일 오르는 상황에서 소비자용 낸드 가격이 떨어진다는 게 얼핏 의아할 수 있다. 서울경제는 스마트폰과 PC 가격이 오르자 소비자들이 기기 교체를 미루고 있다는 점에 주목했다. 스마트폰 출하량은 전년 동기 대비 20% 줄어 3분기 기준 14년 만에 최저치를 기록했다. 시장조사업체 가트너(Gartner)에 따르면 PC 출하량도 전년 동기 대비 22.5% 감소했다.

소비자들이 구매를 미루자 기기 제조사들은 기존 재고부터 소진하고 있다. 당장 생산에 필요한 낸드도 이미 확보한 것으로 보인다. 현물시장에서 낸드를 추가로 사들일 수요가 줄면서 반도체 공장에서 새로 출하되는 물량의 가격이 하락하고 있다는 설명이다.

또 하나 눈여겨볼 점은 낸드의 종류에 따라 생산설비가 다르다는 것이다. D램과 낸드 업체들은 AI 수요에 대응하기 위해 소비자용 제품을 생산하던 라인을 고사양 제품용으로 전환해 왔다. D램의 경우 DDR5와 고대역폭메모리(HBM)가 일부 제조 공정을 공유하기 때문에, 업체들은 DDR5 생산능력의 일부를 꾸준히 HBM으로 돌려 왔다.

반면 서울경제가 인용한 뱅크오브아메리카 보고서에 따르면, 낸드는 사정이 다르다. 최근 고집적 낸드는 적층 단수가 300단 안팎에 이르며, 생산에 필요한 장비도 일반 소비자용 낸드에 쓰이는 장비와 상당한 차이가 있다. 따라서 AI 데이터센터의 낸드 수요가 계속 늘더라도 그만큼 소비자용 낸드 공급이 곧바로 줄어드는 것은 아니다.

중국 낸드 제조사 양쯔메모리테크놀로지스(YMTC)의 공급 확대도 가격 하락 압력을 더하고 있다. 서울경제에 따르면 YMTC는 기존 주요 업체들의 점유율을 잠식하며 올해 2분기 낸드 시장에서 14%의 점유율을 차지했다.

이런 흐름이 이어지면 소비자의 가격 부담도 다소 줄어들 수 있다. 서울경제에 따르면 뱅크오브아메리카는 2027년 1분기 PC·스마트폰용 낸드 고정거래가격이 5~10% 하락할 것으로 전망했다. 같은 기간 기업용 낸드 고정거래가격은 대체로 보합세를 유지할 것으로 내다봤다.

낸드 가격 하락이 SSD나 노트북, 스마트폰의 실제 판매가격 인하로 이어질지는 아직 지켜봐야 한다. 낮아진 가격에 조달한 낸드를 탑재한 제품이 매장에 나오기까지도 시간이 걸린다. 다만 AI 수요로 공급이 빠듯한 상황에서, PC를 조립하거나 기기 교체를 기다려 온 소비자에게는 모처럼 반가운 소식이다.

花旗、PNC等美国银行更新协议，使用第三方AI代理的客户即便遭黑客攻击也需自行担责

11 月 19 日，据 TechCrunch 报道，美国第三大商业银行花旗银行（Citibank）于本周更新在线用户协议，向使用第三方 AI 工具处理个人财务的客户明确，相关操作一旦出现问题将由客户自行承担，即便遭遇黑客攻击也不例外。

花旗发言人对 TechCrunch 表示，随着第三方 AI 工具日益普及，银行希望客户理解分享银行凭证或授权此类工具访问账户的风险，并强调选择向第三方 AI 代理开放账户访问权限的客户，需对该类代理所进行的活动负责。报道称，花旗此次更新不仅要求客户对 AI 代理的操作负责，还规定一旦 AI 工具泄露凭证或遭到黑客攻击，黑客利用账户实施的行为同样由客户承担责任。美国最大的两家银行摩根大通（JPMorgan）和美国银行（Bank of America）已于上月宣布类似政策；美国第八大银行 PNC 于 18 日更新了相关条款。另据 TechCrunch 所见邮件，大型银行 Citizens 本周也向客户发送邮件，警示其需对 AI 助手的所有操作承担责任。

报道指出，AI 代理可被授予银行及其他在线金融门户的登录凭证，用于分析消费和投资、提供建议，乃至处理交易和账单支付。金融机构表示，不会为自动助手发起的有意或无意交易承担撤销责任。Anthropic 本月早些时候推出的个人理财工具被明确标为「只读」，「不能转移、管理或投资用户的资金」。

Кейс. 8,5 млн рублей из России в США. Один лишний банк мог всё усложнить

К нам обратилась семейная пара, которая выиграла грин-карту. Клиенты продали квартиру в Красногорске за 8 500 000 ₽ и планировали перевести полученные деньги на свой счёт в Bank of America.

Первоначально они хотели отправить средства из России в Армению, затем в Израиль и только после этого в США.

Мы предложили изменить маршрут и перевести деньги из Армении сразу в американский банк.

Какое решение мы нашли 👇

1️⃣ Сопроводили удалённое открытие счёта в России

➡️ Мы помогли дистанционно открыть клиенту личный счёт в российском банке 
➡️ Согласовали льготный банковский курс конвертации рублей в валюту.

Это позволило подготовить деньги к международному переводу без поездки в Россию для открытия счёта.

2️⃣ Сопроводили удалённое открытие счёта в Армении

Следующим этапом стало дистанционное открытие личного счёта в армянском банке.

Этот счёт использовали для поступления средств из России и дальнейшего перевода в США.

3️⃣ Исключили лишний этап через Израиль

Клиенты рассчитывали сначала зачислить деньги на свой счет в Израиле, а затем отправить их в Bank of America.

❗️Израильские банки не любят выступать транзитным звеном, например, дальнейший перевод денег в США предполагал ожидание в течение года и дополнительные расходы. 

📍Для клиентов, которым деньги были нужны в Америке, такой маршрут не подходил. Поэтому мы рекомендовали отправить средства напрямую из Армении в США.

4️⃣ Сопроводили перевод в Bank of America

Главное опасение клиента было связано с комплаенсом американского банка: примет ли он крупную сумму от продажи российской недвижимости и какие документы запросит?

В итоге маршрут выглядел так:

🇷🇺 Россия → 🇦🇲 Армения → 🇺🇸 США

✅ Вся сумма перевода успешно поступила на счёт клиентов в Bank of America. Дополнительных документов, подтверждающих происхождение средств, американский банк в этом случае не запросил.

Что важно в этом кейсе?

Дополнительная страна в маршруте не всегда помогает решить задачу. Иногда она добавляет расходы и ограничения. Здесь отказ от промежуточного перевода через Израиль позволил направить деньги сразу в страну, где клиенты планировали ими пользоваться.

Всю банковскую часть, от удалённого открытия счетов и льготной конвертации до сопровождения перевода, мы организовали дистанционно.

Major Banks Drop Fraud Protection for AI Agent Users

Citibank, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and other major US banks now hold customers liable for losses from third-party AI agents, while exempting their own in-house assistants.

  •  Citibank's updated Online User Agreement treats any activity by a third-party AI agent as directly authorized by the customer.
  •  JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America barred outside AI tools from logging in with customer credentials in October and hold users accountable.
  •  Citibank's revised terms exempt its own native AI tools, which analysts link to banks protecting revenue from fee-spotting, cash-sweeping agents.

A Timeshare Tycoon Began America's Biggest House in 2004 — He Died 21 Years Later, Still Unfinished

In 2004, timeshare tycoon David Siegel began building Versailles, a 90,000-square-foot palace on a man-made hill above Lake Butler in Windermere, Florida, just minutes from Walt Disney World. It is bigger than the White House and was meant to be the biggest home in America, with Brazilian mahogany doors, a stained-glass dome that reportedly took three years to build, a bowling alley, a roller rink and a garage for 35 cars. Twenty-one years later, on April 5, 2025, Siegel died at 89, and the house was still not finished.

This is the full story of how one fortune, built on the credit machine behind Westgate Resorts, ran into the 2008 financial crisis, a $65 million listing that drew no buyer, a Bank of America foreclosure threat, the Sundance-winning documentary The Queen of Versailles, the death of the Siegels' daughter, a pandemic, more than $10 million in damage from Hurricane Ian, railings stuck behind tariffs and, in 2026, a contractor's lawsuit seeking to foreclose on a construction lien.

Bank Denied Your Debit Card Fraud Claim? Ask for This in Writing

If your bank denies a debit card dispute, Regulation E says the denial must come with a written explanation and must tell you that you can ask for the documents it relied on. Ask in writing, and it has to send copies promptly, in a form you can understand. The bank gets 10 business days to investigate, and longer (up to 45 days, or 90 for card purchases) only if it credits your money back while it looks. Report a lost or stolen card within 2 business days and your liability is capped at $50; after that, up to $500.
Regulation E covers unauthorized transfers. Money you sent to a scammer yourself usually isn't covered.

From donor-advised funds and family foundations to the growing involvement of Millennials and Gen Z in volunteering, fundraising, and nonprofit leadership, the conversation highlights how the next generation is helping reshape philanthropy. They also discuss concerning trends in declining donor participation, the encouraging rebound in volunteerism, and the importance of celebrating incremental progress. A.P. Giannini & The Bank of America Earthquake Rescue

After watching big banks refuse loans to hardworking fishermen and bricklayers, A.P. Giannini opened the Bank of Italy in a converted San Francisco saloon in 1904, believing a person's character was real collateral.

When the devastating 1906 earthquake and fires struck, Giannini loaded his bank's gold and cash into a borrowed produce wagon, hid it beneath crates of oranges, and drove 18 miles past looters. While rival banks kept their heat-warped vaults locked for months, he set a wooden plank across two barrels on the wharf and lent money to rebuild the city on a signature alone.

The Outages Kept Coming — and Trump Shrugged

The outages kept coming — and Trump shrugged.

Monday, the country's biggest banks went down — Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, Truist. Customers couldn't log in, couldn't see their balances, couldn't move money. Chase says it was a software bug in its own hardware — not a cyberattack — and by this morning, the banks say they're back to normal. But the banks were only the latest. Friday, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop — four and a half hours, thousands of flights cancelled or delayed — after a communications failure in the air traffic control system. Duffy says 17 of the FAA's 22 control centers were running on old routers. Microsoft's Outlook and Teams went down too, and a United tech failure delayed about 150 flights. Now the other side. Nobody has shown these outages are connected — Reuters reports they are not believed to be linked — and the money never went anywhere. But the politics landed today. Asked about the failures, President Trump told reporters in Manila, quote, "It's like when you're big and powerful, and you have all the money. Things like that happen. It's fine." And asked Monday if he takes responsibility for the ground stop, he said, quote, "I don't take any responsibility." His team has asked Congress for 50 billion dollars to overhaul air traffic control — Democrats point out 12 and a half billion was already approved last year, and ask why so much of it is still unspent. And one more thing today: that nationwide emergency alert test at 2:20 — radio and TV only, about a minute, routine, required by law. FEMA said it out loud Monday: "No blackouts, no secret emergencies" — because viral posts spent the week claiming a 90-day blackout starts today. It doesn't. So the question is: is this just a bad week of bad luck — or a warning that the systems we all depend on are thinner than they look?

GTA 6 Price Was a Bank's Idea!?

A Bank of America analyst told Rockstar to set the GTA 6 price at $80 so Call of Duty could charge it too.

This short covers Omar Dessouky, the Bank of America analyst who argued the GTA 6 price should be $80 for the good of the entire industry. His logic was simple: if GTA 6 launched at $70, every other publisher would struggle to justify $80. You walk away knowing who the GTA 6 price was really set for.

The take: a bank asked Rockstar to raise the GTA 6 price so the rest of the industry could raise theirs, and Take-Two went along with it. The objection is that analysts say things all the time and Rockstar does not take orders from Bank of America. Fair, but Take-Two landed exactly where the analyst said it should, and Take-Two has moved the price floor before. When the GTA 6 price matches a Wall Street wish list to the dollar, the people buying were not the only audience. For scale, GTA 5 launched at $59.99 when $60 was the ceiling, and GTA 5 never needed a bank to explain its price.

For context, GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The GTA 6 price is $79.99 for the Standard Edition and $99.99 for the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition. GTA 5 launched in September 2013 at $59.99, which is roughly $86 in today's money, so on paper the GTA 6 price is the cheapest a new Grand Theft Auto has ever been. Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson told the New York Times his own playthrough took about 80 hours, against roughly 31 hours for the GTA 5 main story. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick called the price a bargain on CNBC, and Take-Two was the first major publisher to put a $69.99 standard edition on shelves, with NBA 2K21 in 2020. Every GTA 6 physical copy is a download code in a box, and two retailers, Video Games Plus in Canada and Loot Box Gaming in Delaware, said they will not stock it. Before the reveal, Bank of America analyst Omar Dessouky argued Rockstar should charge $80 so the rest of the industry could follow.

If you searched how much is GTA 6, it is $79.99 for Standard and $99.99 for the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition, and the Ultimate tier adds five single-player businesses in Vice City. If you searched why is GTA 6 $80, the short version is that Rockstar and Take-Two set the GTA 6 price for the whole industry as much as for you. If you searched is GTA 6 worth $80, the per-hour math says yes, roughly a dollar an hour across an 80-hour campaign, while the ownership math says you are buying a license. And because of the GTA 6 no disc decision, a GTA 6 physical copy cannot be resold once the code is redeemed, which GTA 5 discs always could. Searches for how much is GTA 6 and why is GTA 6 $80 both jumped after the reveal, and the answer to both is in how Rockstar and Take-Two framed the number, not the number itself. The GTA 6 no disc question is the one that will outlast launch week.

A note on how these numbers were checked. The roughly $86 figure is an inflation adjustment of the $59.99 GTA 5 launch price from 2013, and depending on which month of consumer price data you use it lands in the mid-$80s. GTA 5 went on to sell across three console generations, which is part of why its $60 tag looked so cheap by the end, and part of why Rockstar can argue that one big purchase lasts a decade. The 80-hour figure comes from Rockstar North and should be read as one developer's playthrough, not an average, while the GTA 5 number of about 31 hours is the commonly cited main-story average. Take-Two has not changed the price since pre-orders opened in June, and nothing announced so far suggests a disc version is coming later. So the question of is GTA 6 worth $80 comes down to what you value: hours, ownership, or the precedent. This channel's position is that GTA 6 can be worth it and still be a bad sign for everyone else, and every short in this series takes one piece of that argument apart. The GTA 6 price itself is not going anywhere.

Bank Outage: Chase Says a Software Bug Did It

World news today, 17 Nov 2026: bank outage. Chase bank outage: JPMorgan Chase says a software bug, not a cyber attack, slowed payments on Monday.

On Monday 16 November, thousands of customers of Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank and other US banks reported problems with online and mobile banking on Downdetector: balances, transfers and sign-ins. Some Chase branches could not complete transactions. By about 2 p.m. Eastern time, Chase had more than 4,700 reports, the most of any bank. Zelle payments were delayed for some users. (CBS News, NBC News, Newsweek, Fox 26)

JPMorgan Chase said the cause was "a software bug in on-premise hardware systems", not a cyber attack. Other banks were slowed only when they were part of a transaction with Chase. Chase said customers still had access to their accounts and funds, and that it worked to fix the issue by the end of Monday. Capital One said it was not affected. (Yahoo Finance, NBC News, CBS News)

What we know so far: at the time of this video, Chase had not said the issue was fully fixed. The outage came days after the Microsoft Outlook outage and the FAA's nationwide ground stop. There is no evidence the incidents are connected. (NBC News, CBS News)

What you can do: the problem is inside Chase's own systems, so reinstalling the app does not fix it. Check Chase's official channels for updates, not unsolicited emails.

No picture of the outage itself is shown: the photos are file photos, and the server video is a data center that is not Chase's.

The card survived, and in 1976 it was renamed Visa.

Stablecoins Are Coming to Your Bank: 5 Changes

Your bank is about to hand you a dollar that is not a dollar. It looks like a dollar. It spends like a dollar. But it pays you nothing, and the government will not insure it. And there is one catch that decides whether it helps you, or hurts you.

- Maya is 34, earns $87,460 a year, and has $25,000 saved. On January 18, 2027, the GENIUS Act switches on, and her bank can hand her its own digital dollar — a stablecoin. This is the story of the five changes coming to her money.
- Change one, the law: the GENIUS Act was signed July 18, 2025, the first federal stablecoin law in America. Only a permitted issuer can make a payment stablecoin, every coin must be backed one-to-one, and every issuer must publish a monthly reserve report. The OCC's final rule landed October 21, 2026. Bank of America has committed to issue one, with no launch date; a 21-bank consortium aims to launch in the first half of 2027. JPMorgan's JPMD is a tokenized deposit, not a stablecoin.
- Change two, the speed: a stablecoin settles in seconds, Friday night, Sunday morning — the network never closes. Maya sends her rent on Friday night, and it lands Friday night.
- Change three, the yield catch: the GENIUS Act says an issuer may not pay any interest or yield to holders — the coin pays zero, by law. Maya's $25,000 earns about $92.50 a year in savings (0.37%), about $1,067.50 a year in a money-market fund (4.27%) — and zero dollars in her bank's coin.
- Change four, the safety catch: a stablecoin is NOT FDIC insured — the $250,000 guarantee does not cover it. In March 2023, USDC fell to $0.87 for a weekend when $3.3 billion of its reserves were stuck in the failed Silicon Valley Bank.
- Change five, the 5 checks: permitted issuer? One-to-one reserves plus a monthly attestation? Redemption at par on demand? No "insured" marketing? Only money you can afford to have frozen for a weekend? The copy playbook: speed in the coin, savings in the fund, checks before everything.
Plus what happens next: the 21-bank consortium aims to launch in the first half of 2027, foreign-issued coins face a cutoff from July 18, 2028, Citigroup projects a $1.9 trillion to $4 trillion market by 2030, and Bank of America's CEO, citing studies, says upwards of $6 trillion in deposits could flow out of banks into stablecoins.

The $67.5M Man Who Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis

Countrywide's toxic mortgages helped trigger the 2008 financial crisis. Angelo Mozilo called his own loans "toxic" in private emails — then settled with the SEC for $67.5 million and never spent a day in jail.

Countrywide Financial, founded in 1969 by Angelo Mozilo and David Loeb, became America's largest mortgage lender — servicing around $1.5 trillion in loans across roughly 9 million mortgages. Its originate-to-sell model bundled mortgages into mortgage-backed securities and sold them to Wall Street, so the risk moved on and the cash came back. In six years it handed out around $2.2 trillion in home loans, as reported. Mozilo's own internal emails called the loan products "toxic" and "poison" — the core of the SEC's securities-fraud allegation. The "Friends of Angelo" VIP unit (1991–2008) gave preferential mortgages to legislators, congressional staffers and lobbyists. Bank of America bought Countrywide in 2008 and by 2012 its total Countrywide bill had passed $40 billion, as reported.

KEY FACTS (as reported):
- Founded 1969 by Angelo Mozilo and David Loeb; America's largest mortgage lender at its peak, servicing ~$1.5T in loans across ~9M mortgages; in 2007 alone it wrote $408B in new mortgages.
- Originate-to-sell model: write mortgages, bundle them into mortgage-backed securities, sell to Wall Street — risk passed on, cash recycled into more loans. In six years it handed out ~$2.2T in home loans, as reported.
- Mozilo's internal emails called the company's loan products "toxic" and "poison" while public filings reassured investors — the SEC's core securities-fraud allegation.
- "Friends of Angelo" VIP unit (1991–2008) gave preferential mortgages to legislators, congressional staffers, lobbyists and other influential figures.
- 4 June 2009: SEC charged Mozilo with securities fraud and insider trading. 15 Oct 2010: he settled for $67.5M ($22.5M penalty + $45M disgorgement, no admission of wrongdoing) and a lifetime ban from serving as an officer/director of any public company — then the largest SEC penalty against a senior executive. Bank of America paid $20M of it under an indemnification agreement.
- Jan 2008: Bank of America agreed to buy Countrywide for ~$4B in stock (closed at ~$2.5B); by 2012 BofA's total Countrywide bill had passed $40B, as reported.
- Aug 2014: BofA paid a record $16.65B DOJ settlement ($9.65B cash + $7B homeowner relief) over mortgage-backed securities tied to Countrywide and Merrill Lynch — then the largest civil settlement with a single entity in US history. Plus $8.5B (2011) and a $1.27B "Hustle" fraud penalty.
- Mozilo was NEVER criminally charged — the US Attorney's Office in Los Angeles decided in 2011 not to file criminal charges, and in 2016 the DOJ dropped its planned civil fraud case against him. CNN named him one of the "Ten Most Wanted: Culprits" of the 2008 collapse; Time named him one of the "25 People to Blame." He died 16 July 2023, aged 84, having personally earned more than $400M, as reported.
- The Oscar-winning documentary Inside Job, which features Mozilo throughout, has been viewed around 2.67 million times on YouTube. That film is about the whole 2008 crisis, not Countrywide alone, but Mozilo is one of its central characters.

IMPORTANT: $67.5M is Mozilo's SEC CIVIL settlement (no admission, never criminally charged). $16.65B is Bank of America's DOJ settlement — NEVER present it as Mozilo's fine. The "toxic" emails are real (SEC complaint) — quoted as the SEC alleged, not as a confession of a crime.

What happened: founded in Montgomery, Alabama in 1850 by three brothers from Germany, Lehman Brothers grew from a dry-goods store into one of Wall Street's great banks. Under CEO Richard Fuld it became a mortgage machine — buying subprime lenders, packaging $146 billion of mortgages into securities in 2006 alone, and borrowing $30 for every $1 of its own money. When housing crashed, the losses mounted: a $2.8 billion loss in June 2008, a $3.9 billion loss that September. A court-appointed examiner later found Lehman had used an accounting device called Repo 105 to move up to $50 billion off its balance sheet at quarter-ends. Over the weekend of 12–14 September 2008, Bank of America walked away to buy Merrill Lynch instead, and a Barclays rescue was blocked by British regulators. At 1:45 a.m. on Monday 15 September 2008, Lehman filed for Chapter 11: $639 billion in assets, $613 billion in debts — the largest bankruptcy in American history. The Dow fell 504 points that day. Within 24 hours the Federal Reserve lent $85 billion to rescue insurer AIG, and within weeks Congress passed a $700 billion rescue package. No Lehman executive was ever charged with a crime.

In this video, I run the exact math across every 2027 Atmos change and all five Atmos cards ($95 Ascent, $395 Summit, $95 Business, future $0 card, and the Cross River Debit Card) so you know which card deserves a spot in your wallet and which ones lose to a free 2% cash back card.

• Fee Hikes & Cuts: Saver and partner Basic Economy earn 0 points. Partner award fees jump 60% from $12.50 to a non-refundable $20 each way ($80 lost canceling for two) unless paid with Summit.
• Status Cuts: Silver loses extra legroom at booking (48-hr window), Gold drops the chocolate bar, 10K/30K Wi-Fi passes end (discount rises $25 to $50), 55K upgrades drop 4 to 2, and Lounge+ / 50K bonus moves from 125K to 150K.
• Free Communities: Families on the Go gives 20% points back for kids 12 and under; Global Locals adds 10% status points internationally + 1 status pt per 25 pts transferred from Bilt or Marriott.
• $95 Ascent Year-Two Math: The $99 Companion Fare takes $6,000/yr spend (~$220 out of pocket with fee and taxes), while $6,000 on a 2% card (Citi Double Cash or Wells Fargo Active Cash) pays $120 cash.
• $395 Summit Math: 3x on Alaska, Hawaiian, dining, and foreign purchases (3.3x with BofA checking), 10,000 annual status pts + 1 status pt per $2 spent, $120 Global Entry credit, $50 delay voucher, and a 25K Global Companion Award (~$375 saved on two 60K awards). The 100K Award needs $60,000 spend ($1,200 opportunity cost on a 2% card).
• Atmos Debit Skip: $6.99/mo ($85/yr) or $2,000 at 0% (~$80/yr lost vs 4% HYSA). Even with a $50 code you start ~$30 behind, and $12K/yr at 0.5x earns ~$90 vs $240 cash on a 2% card.

• 2027 vs 2028 Reality Check: Free Starlink Wi-Fi and the two-floor Seattle lounge arrive in 2027; lie-flat 787/A330 suites, Premium Reserve, and Honolulu/San Diego lounges slip to 2028.

THE WALLET STRATEGY RULES:

2. Family & Partner Flyers: Join Families on the Go or Global Locals immediately, and evaluate the $395 Summit if you easily redeem the 25K Global Companion Award while avoiding $20 partner fees.
3. Wait on 2028 Hype & Refreshes: Hold off on the $95 Business card before its late-2026 refresh, skip the Debit card, and wait for Bank of America's 2027 transfer ratios before shifting spend.

Debit vs Credit Card: The Federal Fraud Trap You Must Know #shorts

Using your debit card for everyday purchases could wipe out your checking account before you even notice.

Whether you bank with JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, or online banks, understanding federal card liability protections is essential to safeguarding your liquid cash.

Key Educational Takeaways:
• Under the Fair Credit Billing Act (Regulation Z), unauthorized credit card liability is capped at $50, with major card networks offering zero liability.
• Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (Regulation E), debit card fraud drains your actual checking account cash immediately.
• If debit fraud is reported after 2 business days, statutory liability jumps to $500; after 60 calendar days from statement delivery, you can lose all stolen funds.
• Using credit cards for daily purchases, gas pumps, and online shopping keeps your primary bank deposits isolated from fraud holds.

• Federal Trade Commission (FTC) - Lost or Stolen Credit, ATM, and Debit Cards
• Federal Reserve Board - Regulation E (12 CFR Part 1005 - Electronic Fund Transfers)
• Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) - 12 CFR § 1026.12 (Regulation Z Special Rules for Credit Cards)

AI Agents Got Into Bank Accounts. Now What?

An AI agent logs in to your bank with your username and your password. To the bank, it looks exactly like you.

That's not a hypothetical. Reporting from Axios (Oct 22, 2026) said major U.S. banks are finding unvetted AI agents operating inside customer accounts — in most cases because customers handed an AI assistant their own login details. Some agents reportedly went further, contacting bank call centers and taking steps beyond what the user asked for.

The banks are responding. Morgan Stanley has blocked third-party agents from its platforms. Bank of America is limiting agent access to consumer deposits. JPMorgan, Citi and Schwab are restricting them too. But almost none are banning AI outright: the line being drawn is between reading your account and acting in it. Read-only access mostly stays open. Moving money is what's being locked down.

The real problem: a password can't tell a bank who is acting — and if your agent sends money you didn't intend to send, you may have a much harder time getting it back.

What to do:
1. Don't give an AI agent your bank password.
2. If you want AI help with money, use official, read-only connections through your bank's approved partners.
3. For anything that moves money, keep a human approval step.
4. Expect this to change — banks know customers will want agents, and they're looking for a middle ground.

When you compare AI assistants, check what each one actually connects to, and how. That's the kind of trade-off we lay out at navigateaitools.com.

On the morning of February 28, 1997, two men in homemade body armor walked into a Bank of America branch on Laurel Canyon Boulevard in North Hollywood, carrying illegally converted automatic rifles. KEY FACTS
Robbers: Larry Phillips Jr. (26) and Emil Mătăsăreanu (30), who met at a Gold's Gym in 1989 and were arrested together in Glendale in 1993 with weapons and armor. Bank: Bank of America, 6600 Laurel Canyon Blvd. The robbers went in around 9:16 a.m. as Officers Loren Farrell and Martin Perello drove past and radioed it in; the shooting ended just after 10:00 a.m. Robbers fired an estimated 1,100 rounds, police about 650. 12 officers and 8 civilians were injured; no officer or bystander was killed. Officers borrowed AR-15 rifles and ammunition from B&B Sales. Phillips died on Archwood Street of a self-inflicted wound as he was struck by police fire. Mătăsăreanu was wounded about 29 times and died before paramedics reached him; his family's 2000 federal lawsuit ended in a hung jury and was dropped, and whether he could have been saved is still debated. Seven months later, the Department of Defense gave the LAPD 600 surplus M16 rifles; 18 officers received the Medal of Valor and met President Bill Clinton in 1998.

The ENTIRE History of Mastercard in 25 Minutes

The history of Mastercard and the Karl Hinke story: how a nervous club of rival bankers in Buffalo, New York became a payments network worth close to $590 billion, without ever lending you a single dollar. This documentary argues that Mastercard was never really built on plastic, but on an agreement between banks that did not trust each other, and on the tiny toll it collects every time money moves.

Mastercard was built by a committee. The man most often named as its creative force is Karl H. Hinke, a Buffalo banker who started his career in 1930, as thousands of American banks collapsed in the Great Depression. He learned one lesson there: a single bank can fall, but a group of banks that agree on shared rules can survive almost anything. In 1966, when Bank of America offered to turn every other bank into a BankAmericard franchise, Hinke rallied rival bankers to build the opposite, a network that nobody owned and everybody shared.

Today there are about 3.8 billion Mastercard and Maestro cards in the world, nearly one for every two people alive. Between 2003 and 2008, Mastercard agreed to pay roughly $3.7 billion in antitrust settlements to Wal-Mart, American Express and Discover, more than its entire 2003 revenue. And a single share bought at the $39 IPO price in 2006 is worth roughly $6,700 today, before dividends.

This documentary follows the complete history of Mastercard: Karl H. Hinke joins Marine Midland in Buffalo in 1930, Bank of America and the BankAmericard, the founding of the Interbank Card Association on August 16, 1966, Master Charge in California, the Master Charge name bought from a small company in Kentucky, Citibank and the Everything Card, the 1969 bankers' convention in Hawaii, John D. Bellinger and First Hawaiian Bank, the Chicago unsolicited card mailings, the 1970 ban on unsolicited credit cards, the 1979 rename to MasterCard, the Priceless campaign, the Wal-Mart "honor all cards" lawsuit, the Department of Justice case, the 2006 NYSE IPO, the American Express and Discover settlements, the 2008 financial crisis, interchange and swipe fees, the network effect, Ajay Banga, Vocalink, the European Commission fine, Michael Miebach, the Merricks UK class action, the $38 billion swipe fee settlement, BVNK, stablecoins and AI shopping agents.

Critics argue that two card networks control most American card payments and that swipe fees, which a merchant coalition puts at about $119 billion in 2025, end up in prices everyone pays. Mastercard says those fees pay for guaranteed payment, fraud protection and a system that works in more than two hundred countries and territories in about a second.

So the next time you tap your card and hear that short, bright beep, remember what it really is. Thousands of banks, scattered across the planet, agreeing in one second that you are good for it. Some things money can't buy. Trust is one of them, and Mastercard found a way to charge a toll on it.

This documentary is built on company filings, annual reports, books and verified reporting.

BCCI: The Day Regulators Shut Down a Global Bank

The Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) was shut down on July 5, 1991, after regulators uncovered an extensive pattern of financial deception.

Across multiple countries, accounts were frozen, and customers who trusted the bank suddenly lost access to their money.

Founded in 1972 by Pakistani banker Agha Hassan Abedi, BCCI grew into an international banking empire operating in more than 70 countries. It served ordinary depositors, businesses, and wealthy investors while senior figures concealed financial losses, used offshore companies to obscure transactions, and secretly gained control of American banks.

This documentary investigates the rise and collapse of BCCI, from its connections to Middle Eastern wealth and its hidden acquisition of First American to the Gokal family's troubled loans and the bank's relationship with Panamanian leader Manuel Noriega.

We examine Operation SeaChase, which exposed money laundering connected to drug trafficking, the intelligence concerning BCCI's secret ownership of American banks, and the regulatory failures that allowed the institution to survive despite years of warning signs.

The investigation culminates in the Price Waterhouse Sandstorm Report and the coordinated closure of BCCI in July 1991.

But the consequences did not end when the bank closed. Depositors, employees, and small businesses faced years of financial uncertainty while courts and liquidators attempted to recover billions of dollars.

BCCI's history reveals how an institution built around international opportunity became a case study in financial fraud, political influence, secrecy, and the limits of banking regulation.

The Bank That Mailed 60,000 Credit Cards Nobody Asked For

In 1958, Bank of America mailed 60,000 credit cards to people in Fresno who never asked for one. No application, no interview, no banker across the desk. Here is how that mailing created the modern credit card, and why paying with one still doesn't feel like spending.

Before the card, borrowing meant sitting in front of a loan officer and asking for permission. Joseph Williams and a small team at Bank of America thought there was a faster way: skip the application and put the credit in people's hands first. They signed up 300 Fresno merchants, mailed the cards, and introduced revolving credit, where you pay part of the bill and the rest carries over with interest.

It nearly collapsed. Around 22% of accounts fell behind, thieves raided mailboxes, and losses approached $9 million. Yet the program survived, spread across California, became Visa, and pushed Congress to ban unsolicited card mailings in 1970. Along the way, it removed something no one priced in: the face of the person you owed.

BCCI Bank Scandal: No Auditor Saw It All — Confessions Vol. XXXII

The bcci bank scandal is the story of the Bank of Credit and Commerce International, a bank in 78 countries that no single auditor was ever allowed to see whole.
On July 5, 1991, regulators closed it in a single coordinated day, with about a million depositors' savings inside.

RESOURCES — The 8K Finance · Confessions: we read the primary filings so you don't have to. Every number in this episode traces to the free primary sources listed below — SEC EDGAR, court records, and regulator releases. No paid sponsors or affiliate links on this episode.
📄 CASE FILE PDF: the one-page case file for this episode (filings + timeline) joins the Confessions library with the series relaunch — this description gets the real link in plain text the day it exists. No placeholder links, ever.

TL;DW: The Bank of Credit and Commerce International was founded in 1972 by Agha Hasan Abedi, registered in Luxembourg with head offices in Karachi and London; Bank of America took 25 percent of the founding capital. The group was built around BCCI SA (Luxembourg, 1972) and BCCI Overseas (Cayman Islands, 1975). A decade after opening: over 400 branches in 78 countries, assets in excess of $20 billion, the seventh largest private bank in the world. Its audits were split: Ernst & Whinney audited only the holding company and Luxembourg, Price Waterhouse only Cayman Overseas; neither could audit all operations, for over a decade. A single accountant was ordered in 1985; from 1987 the consolidated audit still excluded ICIC, KIFCO and BCP, some secretly owned. Treasury fraud was found in January 1986; $430 million of treasury losses surfaced by June 1986. Operation C-Chase ended in Tampa indictments in October 1988; the bank later pleaded guilty to money laundering. In 1990 the audit revealed $1.48 billion of loans to its own shareholders, collateralised by its own stock; losses of $498 million for 1989 were announced, Abu Dhabi took control with 77 percent, and Abedi and Swaleh Naqvi resigned on October 4, 1990. In June 1991 the Section 41 report described accounts falsified over the last decade, with about $600 million unrecorded. On July 5, 1991 regulators in seven countries locked down branch records; the Federal Reserve imposed a $200 million fine. About a million depositors worldwide, about 6,500 in Britain, had money inside; local authorities alone lost £78 million. On its own separate line, the court record estimated overall deficiencies in excess of $10 billion. The Bingham report was published on October 22, 1992, and the Senate's Kerry Report in December 1992. Previous volume, Vol. XXXI, Barings Collapse: £827M in Account 88888, is live in the Confessions playlist: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oW-yb5YmBw8 — next, Vol. XXXIII: Drexel Burnham Lambert, the junk bond firm that fell in 1990.

Реальные события последних дней, которые блогеры объединили в одну «катастрофу», выглядят так:

1. Что действительно сломалось

• Крупнейший авиаколлапс с 2001 года (13–16 ноября). В пятницу, 13 ноября, Федеральное управление гражданской авиации США (FAA) на несколько часов полностью остановило вылеты по всей стране из-за потери связи и сбоя радаров. Причиной стал неисправный маршрутизатор при замене старого оборудования, который перегрузил сеть. За выходные были отменены и задержаны десятки тысяч рейсов, к понедельнику работа аэропортов начала стабилизироваться.


Сбои в крупных банках (16 ноября). В понедельник тысячи клиентов JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo и U.S. Bank не могли зайти в приложения, проверить баланс и отправить переводы через Zelle. В Chase официально заявили, что это локальная программная ошибка в их внутреннем оборудовании, а не кибератака.

Сбой у Microsoft и United Airlines. Незадолго до проблем с авиадиспетчерами фиксировался сбой облачных сервисов Microsoft, а позже — полуторачасовой технический сбой у авиакомпании United. Власти и компании подчеркивают, что эти инциденты не связаны между собой.


Откуда взялись слухи про «блэкаут и обнуление счетов»

Плановый тест тревоги. Реальным поводом для слухов стало обычное тестирование системы экстренного оповещения (Emergency Alert System), которое агентства FEMA и FCC провели 17 ноября. На одну минуту прервалось вещание ТВ и радио для проверки сигнала — никаких отключений электричества или связи не было.

The OCC finalized its GENIUS Act stablecoin rule last month. It covers nearly everything the OCC was required to write, except the part that will be hardest to get right: AML and sanctions compliance.

Tokenization is moving from experiments to real money. Banks are no longer asking whether blockchain belongs in finance. They're asking how to run it under supervision.

Look at the last few weeks:

→ DTCC's Tokenization Service went live in October, with 20 firms signed on, including JPMorgan, Citi, and Bank of America.

→ PNC Bank and Coinbase launched a pilot that lets corporate clients receive USDC, converted automatically into dollars.

→ The OCC's final GENIUS Act rule takes effect January 18, 2027.

But one detail stands out. The OCC's rule leaves out the Bank Secrecy Act, AML, and OFAC sanctions requirements. FinCEN and OFAC proposed those in a separate rule in April, and it's still pending. As proposed, it wouldn't take effect until a year after it's finalized.

The obligations haven't gone away. They're just on a different timeline.

The compliance gap didn't close. It moved.

Five questions every institution moving onto blockchain rails should be able to answer:

→ Screening: Which KYC, AML, and sanctions checks ran on each transaction, and when?

→ Approvals: Who requested and who approved each payment?

→ Examiner access: Can regulators verify activity with selective access, without seeing everything?

→ Data privacy: Can sensitive data stay off-chain while the proof stays on-chain?

→ Future security: How will today's cryptography adapt to quantum threats?

Moving assets on-chain is only the beginning. The hard part is building infrastructure where compliance is part of every transaction, not an audit after the fact.

Compliance belongs in every transaction. That's what we've built at Habify Labs with Omnareth.

Which of these five is the biggest gap for your institution?

Newlab is bringing back its Founder Fellowship for a sixth year, selecting 15 startups working on critical technologies with the ambition to help them move from development toward real-world deployment.

The programme is being run alongside NYCEDC's Venture for NYC initiative, Bank of America and Gunderson Dettmer. Instead of offering a traditional accelerator experience alone, the fellowship is built around practical founder support: workshops, one-on-one mentoring, industry introductions and access to potential pilot and investment opportunities.

Selected startups may also have an opportunity to receive up to $150,000 in investment from Newlab. This is an opportunity-based amount, not guaranteed funding for every participating company.

Newlab's focus is on technologies that can have meaningful industrial and societal impact. The fellowship is particularly aimed at founders from underrepresented backgrounds building in critical technology sectors, helping them access the networks and commercial relationships that are often difficult to establish early in a company's life.

The interesting part of this initiative is the combination of capital access with industry connectivity. For hardware and critical-tech founders, securing a pilot with the right corporate partner can be just as important as raising their next round.

Cohort: 15 startups
Potential investment: Up to $150,000

What happens when AI produces professional insights that management cannot independently evaluate? Who owns the decisions that follow?

On November 18, the Financial Times reported that KPMG tested more than 100 AI agents alongside a conventional audit of an FTSE 250 company.

The experiment was not used for the statutory audit opinion, but it raises an important management question.

As AI enables professional firms to generate deeper, faster insights, how do organizations preserve independent judgment, professional boundaries, and accountability?

In my latest article, I apply Managing Hybrid Intelligence to this challenge.

The focus extends beyond whether AI findings are accurate:

• Does additional analysis fall within the engagement?
• Can management independently evaluate recommendations?
• When does repeated reliance threaten independence?
• Could AI recommendations later inform their own evaluation?
• Do receiving teams have the expertise and authority to act?

Accurate AI analysis does not automatically establish the right business decision.

Industry Perspectives Welcome

🏦 Banking: JPMorganChase, Bank of America, Citi, HSBC. How should institutions preserve independent judgment when external AI analysis influences decisions?

📊 Audit & Professional Services: KPMG US, PwC, Deloitte, EY. How should firms manage independence, cumulative reliance, and human accountability?

⚖️ Governance & Standards: Financial Reporting Council, International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants (IESBA), IFAC. What operational evidence could strengthen existing safeguards?

💻 Technology & Enterprise AI: Microsoft, IBM, Accenture, SAP. How should AI workflows preserve authority and independent verification?

🏭 Manufacturing & Operations: Siemens, Schneider Electric, Unilever. How should management evaluate AI recommendations before consequential changes?

Executive Perspectives Welcome

I welcome insights from CFOs, CEOs, COOs, audit committees, boards, auditors, risk leaders, and governance professionals.

AI can expand organizational intelligence. It must not quietly relocate accountability for how that intelligence is used.

Explore my free TRAIT Framework and Employee Guide, designed for use with an organization-approved AI assistant without new technology purchases or consulting fees:

https://lnkd.in/d6-AM8qu

I welcome independent critique and industry experience.

#ManagingHybridIntelligence #AgenticAI #AuditGovernance #ResponsibleAI #CorporateGovernance

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗻𝗼 𝗹𝗼𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗼𝘀𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗮𝗻𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀?

text:
Bank of America put out its childcare payments data last month. Most people will read the headline, median payments up just 1%. Looks like things are cooling off.

Look one line down. The number of households paying for childcare at all fell 1% from last year. For lower income households it fell 2%. Meanwhile the share paying more than $2,000 a month has more than doubled since 2023.

Those families didn't find cheaper care. A lot of them stopped paying for care. Grandma, a neighbor, or one parent cut hours (reminds me of a NAR article from a couple of years ago that mentioned that the #1 reason for 60+ year olds to relocate was to be closer to grandchildren to help with costs, end tangent). Childcare jobs are down 0.7% too. The families who get priced out stop showing up in the averages. That's how a crisis starts to look stable.

text:
In 2026, the first Baby Boomers turned 80. That is not a forecast. It is a headcount.

According to Census Bureau projections cited by NIC MAP, the population 80 and older is set to grow 36% by 2030 from a 2023 base, or roughly 5.65 million more people. By 2040 it is nearly double.

What has changed is the money around them. Bank of America's Institute, using Federal Reserve data, reported that households age 55 and over held close to $140 trillion in net worth in the second quarter of 2026, around three-quarters of the U.S. total.

AARP's Longevity Economy Outlook puts the broader picture in even starker terms. Adults 50 and over generated $12.5 trillion, or 43% of U.S. GDP. Their households spent $10.7 trillion, 56 cents of every consumer dollar.

I keep coming back to the same gap. The people and the dollars are already in place. A lot of companies are still designing as if the core customer is 35.

That is a mistake, and it is also not the whole story. Wealth inside this group is badly skewed, and healthcare costs remain a real strain for older households on tighter incomes. The longevity economy is large. It is not evenly shared.

That gap, and who is actually building what older Americans need at a price they can pay, is what I write about in The Longevity Economy.

text:
Your AI assistant just moved money out of your account. Your bank will call that your decision.

Citibank updated its online user agreement this week. Customers who hand account access to a third-party AI agent are responsible for everything that agent does, even if the tool leaks their login or gets hacked. TechCrunch reported the change on November 18, 2026. JPMorgan and Bank of America set similar policies in October, and PNC changed its terms the same day.

Be clear about what is still unproven. No court or regulator has tested whether these terms hold up when a real account is drained, and federal rules still cap what a customer can owe for an unauthorized transfer. text:
With all these major technology outages lately, I'm starting to wonder if I should be checking the news or checking my generator and toilet paper inventory!

Between the FAA grounding flights, disruptions involving Microsoft, Bank of America, Apple, and reports of problems at the NSA, it seems like every time you turn around, something else is going down!

And apparently, people are getting nervous enough that they're heading to Costco to stock up on emergency supplies.

Does anybody else remember COVID?

You couldn't find toilet paper, paper towels, or bottled water anywhere!
I'm still not sure why toilet paper becomes the most valuable commodity in America whenever there's a crisis, but apparently, it's right up there with gold!

Now, I don't know whether these recent outages are connected, and there's no established evidence that they are. Officials have attributed various disruptions to technical problems rather than coordinated attacks.

But with AI advancing at an incredible pace and all the talk about superintelligence, I do wonder how prepared we are for something more serious.

And I say that as somebody who's always taken preparedness pretty seriously.
I'm an Eagle Scout, and our motto was simple: Be Prepared.

Apparently, I took that motto a little more seriously than some of my fellow Scouts!
I've got a generator, solar power, batteries, plenty of food and water, and other emergency supplies.

Of course, living in Texas, there are always a few folks who think the answer to every emergency is having 10,000 rounds of ammunition!

I'm all for protecting yourself and your family, but you can't eat bullets, and they won't keep your refrigerator running!

All joking aside, these disruptions do concern me.
Our government, banking systems, airlines, businesses, and practically everything else depend on technology working properly.

What happens if the next major outage affects the electrical grid?
Or our water treatment plants and water distribution systems?
And what if something that normally takes a few hours to fix takes several days or even weeks?

Living in Texas, we've already experienced what happens when the electrical grid has serious problems. It's not much fun!

I'm certainly not predicting some catastrophic event, and I hope these recent incidents are nothing more than unrelated technical failures.

But I do wonder whether we're becoming so dependent on technology that we're not adequately prepared when it fails.

I'd really like to hear what everybody thinks.
Are these outages simply an unfortunate coincidence, or are they warning signs that our infrastructure is becoming increasingly vulnerable?

Do you think AI will make these systems safer and more reliable, or introduce even more risks? And are you personally prepared if the power, internet, or water goes out for an extended period?

I'm genuinely curious what people think about all this.

In the meantime, I'm going to make sure my generator starts, my batteries are charged, and I've got plenty of toilet paper!

text:
Crash and Learn!
Within a few days, several big systems went down: Microsoft email, every departing flight in America, Chase, United and the NSA’s top-secret network. Officials say none of those systems was hacked. The real hack hit Monday, quietly, on websites tied to 178 organizations, including Zoom, CNN and Equifax.
Rough week for anything with a plug.
Thursday, Nov. 12: Outlook and Teams went down in 74 countries for 23 hours and 50 minutes.
Friday, Nov. 13: The FAA stopped every departing flight in America for more than four hours.
Monday, Nov. 16: Chase customers saw “Some services aren’t available” for hours, and Bank of America, Wells Fargo and U.S. Bank customers felt it, too. Then United’s system that calculates each plane’s takeoff weight crashed, delaying 418 flights.
Tuesday, Nov. 17: NSANet, the spy agency’s classified internal network, and a number of Apple services, including its App Store, iCloud and Apple Pay, went offline.
Bugs, not bandits
Hackers? Officials say no. Microsoft says a bug it introduced in July knocked more than 80% of its network gateway servers offline. The FAA traced its mess to a new router a contractor installed that flooded its network.
Chase blamed a software bug, and United says it wasn’t a cyberattack. A source told The Wall Street Journal the NSA was installing a software patch. Apple blamed one of its own internal updates, not hackers, and most services came back within about three hours.
Now for the real hack. Early on Nov. 16, crooks slipped malicious code into Optimizely, a tool companies use to test their websites. Security firm Report URI found it on sites tied to 178 organizations, including Zoom, CNN, Equifax, IKEA and Alaska Airlines. We’re talking major companies.
It copied credit card numbers, expiration dates and security codes typed into sites’ checkout forms. (Separate payment pop-ups were out of reach.) It swapped crypto wallet addresses to steal payments. And it hit older iPhones and iPads with spy tools for simply opening a page. iOS 26.3 or later is protected.
Here’s my take. 
We put our lives in the hands of a few giant systems, and AI writes much of the code that runs them. Google says AI generates 75% of its new code. In a survey, 1 in 4 big company tech teams said AI-written code caused a complete outage.
Nobody has blamed AI for these latest crashes. But code is shipping faster than humans can check it. Until that changes, keep a plan B.
FYI, crooks love an outage. Ignore any “verify your account” text.

text:
Citi changed its online terms this week. If you let a third-party AI tool into your account, whatever it does is on you. So is whatever a hacker does with credentials that leak from that tool. JPMorgan, Bank of America, PNC and Citizens have told customers much the same.
⠀
The banks have a point about one thing. Handing your bank password to an outside service is dangerous.
⠀
But look at where the large breaches in financial services came from this month. At Rakuten Securities, records for up to 4.47 million accounts were in a test environment an outsider got into. In Ireland, a flaw in one supplier's software exposed members of 43 credit unions. In France, about €100 million left Crédit Mutuel Arkéa through a service provider's platform. In none of these did a customer install anything or share a password.
⠀
The new terms cover the case where one account gets hurt, and they name the customer as the party at fault in advance. They say nothing about the cases where millions of accounts get hurt.
⠀
And why does a customer hand over a password in the first place? Because the bank offers no other way to connect an assistant. A password has no "view only" setting and no spending limit.
⠀
This is solvable today. Give the agent a limited right instead of a password: read statements, or pay up to a set amount. And have the agent prove what it is. With confidential computing, the processor signs evidence of which code is running, the bank checks it before each session, and the access key is released only to that verified code. The agent holds nothing worth stealing.

text:
Microsoft. Chase. Bank of America. Wells Fargo. Apple Pay. The FAA. United. Marriott. The NSA's classified comms network. All in the same week.

The natural reaction is to ask whether AI finally took something down. The honest answer is no. Officials say the incidents look unrelated, and there is no evidence a rogue AI was behind any of them. Reporting on the AWS incident earlier this year made the same point: speculation blamed an AI coding tool, and the company said it was human error.

A word on the hysteria, because it is expensive.

When every outage gets blamed on AI, three things happen:
1. Real root causes get missed
2. Good pilots get killed before they prove anything
3. Organizations with genuinely brittle systems get a free pass

Panic is not rigor. Calibrating the risk is.

So here is what these failures actually share:

1. Change velocity. The Microsoft event traced to failed server health checks. Health checks are change. So is every deploy, config push, and policy update behind them.

2. Coupling. Banking systems are interconnected by design. One degraded dependency becomes five degraded services.

3. Unmapped blast radius. Nobody can say with confidence what sits downstream of a service until it goes down.

AI did not cause this wave. But AI is compressing change cycles, generating code faster than review can absorb, and widening blast radius in organizations that never mapped their dependencies.

The right response is not fear. It is discipline: map what you have, test change in a lower environment, and put controls around velocity before you scale it.

That is the difference between a transformation and a headline.

Per TechCrunch, that includes a leaked credential or a hacked agent. Agents Citi provides itself are carved out. PNC changed its terms this week, Citizens emailed customers a similar warning, and JPMorganChase and Bank of America announced similar policies in October.

The carve-out is the tell. Liability lands on whoever can vouch for how the agent behaves. A bank will stand behind an agent it built and controls. It will not stand behind one it cannot observe.

Expect the same clause from your own counterparties. The useful question before connecting an agent is not whether it is capable. It is whether anyone can show how it behaves in your workflow, because the contract already assigns the loss.

text:
America's biggest banks are shutting AI agents out of customer accounts. Not because the agents failed to log in. Because they logged in perfectly.

Axios reported on 22 October that JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley are restricting third party agents that sign in with a customer's own credentials. One bank executive said banks struggle to tell whether an agent has been authorised by the user or has gone rogue. Morgan Stanley says it hasn't seen rogue agents on its platforms and is blocking them as a precaution.

That quote is the whole story. A correct password tells the bank which account. It doesn't tell the bank who sent the agent, what it was allowed to do, or until when.

Some banks are moving to read only access, so an agent can look but can't move money. It's a sensible stopgap. The same executives also say customers will keep asking to use agents, so the question won't go away.

What's missing isn't better bot detection. It's a mandate the customer has signed themselves, tied to a verified person, saying this agent may do this, up to this amount, until this date. Then the bank isn't guessing intent from behaviour. It's checking what the customer actually agreed to.

If you work on fraud or digital channels at a bank: when an agent turns up with valid credentials today, what would it need to show you before you'd let it move money?

text:
Lokale KI am Donnerstag: 4 Dinge, die du wissen solltest 🖥️

Deine Daten bleiben bei dir, und keine Rechnung pro Anfrage. Das hat sich getan:

1. Rechnungen auslesen, ohne sie hochzuladen
Cloudflare hat zwei KI-Modelle frei veröffentlicht, die aus Rechnungen und Belegen genau das herausziehen, was man braucht: Lieferant, Betrag, Datum, einzelne Positionen. Die Lizenz (Apache 2.0) erlaubt auch die Nutzung in Firmen. Das Spannende: Man kann sie auf dem eigenen Server laufen lassen. Rechnungen, Verträge und Spesenbelege müssen also nicht mehr zu einem Online-Dienst, das freut jeden, der an die DSGVO denkt.
Aber: Bisher braucht es Python und eine Nvidia-Grafikkarte, eine einfache Klick-Version gibt es noch nicht, und ob deutsche Rechnungen gut klappen, ist nicht bekannt.

2. Ein großes Modell aus China passt jetzt auf einen 64-GB-Rechner
Tencent hat sein Modell Hy4-flash zum Herunterladen freigegeben. Es ist riesig, rechnet aber pro Wort nur mit einem kleinen Teil, und ein großes Stück darf auf der Festplatte bleiben. Ein Entwicklerteam hat es so stark verkleinert, dass rund 49 GB Arbeitsspeicher reichen.
Der Preis-Check: Ein Mac mini mit 64 GB Arbeitsspeicher kostet auf geizhals.at ab 2.938,36 €. Einmal gekauft, laufen solche Modelle ohne Abo und ohne Internet.
Aber: Das geht bisher nur mit einer Vorab-Version der Software llama.cpp, die kleine Version verliert spürbar an Qualität, und auf dem Mac ist sie noch nicht getestet.

3. Stimmen aus verrauschten Aufnahmen retten
Die Firma Inworld hat ein kleines, frei nutzbares Modell veröffentlicht, das Stimmen von Hintergrundlärm trennt. Es läuft sogar auf einem normalen Prozessor ohne Grafikkarte. Ein Reddit-Nutzer erzählt, er habe damit die einzige alte Aufnahme seines verstorbenen Vaters hörbar gemacht, damit sein Sohn den Opa einmal hören kann. Solche Aufnahmen will man nicht auf irgendeinen Server laden, und das muss man jetzt auch nicht.
Aber: Bisher ist es ein Werkzeug für die Kommandozeile, noch keine fertige App.

4. Festplatten könnten bald günstiger werden
Die Preise für Speicherchips, aus denen SSDs gebaut werden, sind laut einem Bericht innerhalb eines Monats um etwa 20 % gefallen. Die Bank of America erwartet Anfang 2027 etwas günstigere Preise für PC- und Handy-Speicher. Für lokale KI ist das gut, denn Modelle werden groß und liegen auf der SSD. Kleiner Tipp für Windows-Nutzer mit Nvidia-Karte: Die neuesten Treiber schreiben laut Berichten im Leerlauf ständig Daten auf die SSD, ein älterer Treiber (621.01) soll das Problem nicht haben.
Aber: Ob die günstigeren Chips wirklich im Laden ankommen, ist noch offen.

Lokale KI wird praktischer, gerade für Dinge, die privat bleiben sollen.

text:
Uma empresa de cibersegurança utilizou inteligência artificial (IA) para descobrir uma vulnerabilidade crítica na popular linguagem de programação Java.

O Java é uma linguagem popular, utilizada pela maioria das principais empresas do mundo, como a Apple e a Amazon, além de muitos bancos, governos e hospitais.

Seu objetivo é fazer com que o mundo da informática gerencie a memória online com mais segurança, segundo o professor e cientista da computação Toby Walsh. E é por isso que "esta é uma falha tão grave e improvável", explica ele.

Na terça-feira (17/11), a Agência de Segurança Nacional dos Estados Unidos (NSA, na sigla em inglês) informou que suas comunicações internas ficaram fora de serviço devido a uma "manutenção programada de rotina".

A agência não especificou se a interrupção dos serviços tinha relação com o erro detectado na linguagem Java.

Com ajuda da IA, a Calif descobriu uma grave vulnerabilidade de segurança, batizada por eles de Java4Shell. Ela permitia a um adversário executar remotamente comandos indesejados no sistema de memória do Java.

A Oracle, proprietária do Java, publicou na terça-feira (17/11) uma "atualização crítica" que, segundo a empresa, contém correções de vulnerabilidades de segurança, incluindo a falha recém-descoberta.

Mas a vulnerabilidade do Java continua sendo uma grande preocupação para os especialistas em cibersegurança. Eles afirmam que sobrecarregar a memória de um sistema é um dos meios mais comuns utilizados pelos hackers para explorar ou derrubar um sistema.

A investigação da Calif indicou que a linguagem de programação e o sistema de informática, lançados pela primeira vez em 1995, são, agora, o "motor da economia moderna".

Uma das suas principais funções é gerenciar e proteger a memória, declarou à BBC o destacado pesquisador especializado em inteligência artificial Toby Walsh.

Toda vez que transferimos informações via internet, recebemos um arquivo de um usuário ou precisamos iniciar sessão em um sistema de informática com uma senha, a plataforma sendo utilizada provavelmente depende de um programa em Java.

Esta grave falha poderia comprometer "sistemas financeiros críticos, dados de clientes e de organizações", afirma o especialista em cibersegurança Pedram Hayati.

Os incidentes mais recentes deixam claro que praticamente todos os setores críticos, incluindo os sistemas de segurança nacional, a aviação e as telecomunicações, dependem de infraestruturas obsoletas na internet.

No início desta semana, milhares de clientes dos principais bancos americanos, como o JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo e Bank of America, informaram sobre problemas de acesso aos seus serviços.

A descoberta sobre o Java surge após uma grave vulnerabilidade de cibersegurança identificada na linguagem de programação PHP, também identificada pela Calif.

Nobody puts this on LinkedIn, so I will.
⠀
It is hard to make a living as a freelance lawyer.
⠀
After 13 years at Bank of America Merrill Lynch, I went independent in 2015.
⠀
I pictured a steady stream of interesting clients who needed a derivatives expert.
⠀
Here is what it actually looked like.
⠀
Projects that lasted a week.
Projects that lasted two months.
A recruiter who told me a big bank project desperately needed my expertise. I signed on. It turned out they did not need me much at all.
Engagements that started with a handshake and then went quiet.
⠀
Feast.
Famine.
Mostly famine.
⠀
I am not writing this to complain.
⠀
Those years taught me things I could not have learned inside a big institution.
⠀
How to walk into an unfamiliar organization and figure out quickly what the business actually needs.
How to be useful without a team behind me.
How to explain complicated derivatives rules to people who had never touched a swap.
⠀
On one project, I was the subject matter expert on new swap margin rules for a global bank, guiding negotiators who had almost no derivatives experience. That project taught me more about teaching than any job title ever did.
⠀
Those years also taught me something about myself.
⠀
I do my best work inside a team.
With structure.
With a mission bigger than the next engagement.
⠀
The best stretch of my recent career was helping launch the FMX Futures Exchange at Cantor Fitzgerald, surrounded by people who wanted the same outcome I did.
⠀
That is what I am building toward next.
⠀
To everyone out there consulting, freelancing, or "between things": you are not alone, and the skills you are building count.
⠀
Have you lived the consultant feast or famine? What did it teach you?

In a Bank of America survey relayed by Fast Company on July 29, 2026, 78% of business owners called succession planning critical.

Only 20% had a fully documented plan.

I read that gap as a problem of format more than belief. Nobody doubts it matters. But "succession plan" is a large phrase, and a large phrase is easy to agree with and hard to start. In my view, it gets easier when you shrink it to a single Tuesday: you don't show up, and you ask what has happened by Friday.

That is the idea behind the Tuesday Plan, which has six rows: Authority, Access, People, Money, Protection and Intent. Authority is who can sign while you're out, Access is who can reach the accounts and systems, and People is who your team and advisors call. Money, Protection and Intent cover what keeps cash moving, what is in force if something happens to you, and what you want, written where someone else can read it. A plan that fills all six rows is what I'd call documented.

What I'd ask you to do this week is draw the six rows on one page, put a name and a date beside each, and see which rows stay blank. Those blanks are the distance between calling succession critical and having it written down.

If several rows stayed empty, the Wealth Command Workshop is one afternoon on Act Two, built on your own numbers, and you leave with a first working wealth plan. The next virtual session is January 9, 2027.

text:
¿Quién responde cuando un agente de IA mueve dinero o sufre un ataque?

Esta semana, Citibank actualizó sus términos de servicio con una definición contundente: los clientes asumen la responsabilidad por los problemas, errores, fraudes o transacciones ejecutadas mediante herramientas de inteligencia artificial de terceros utilizadas para finanzas personales, incluso si la cuenta resulta comprometida por un hackeo.  
No es un caso aislado. 

Entidades como JPMorgan, Bank of America y PNC ya avanzaron en políticas similares frente al avance de asistentes automatizados que reciben credenciales para analizar gastos, sugerir inversiones, pagar facturas o iniciar movimientos de fondos.  

Desde la experiencia operativa y de control en la industria financiera, este movimiento abre varios debates clave para el ecosistema:

Viñeta Gestión del riesgo y delegación de credenciales: entregar claves o permisos a agentes externos de IA rompe esquemas tradicionales de autenticación y trazabilidad. Cuando algo falla, la frontera entre error del algoritmo, brecha de seguridad del tercero y negligencia del usuario se vuelve difusa.  

Viñeta Cobertura y seguros: ¿cómo se redefinen las coberturas de fraude, ciberriesgo y responsabilidad frente a operaciones automatizadas no autorizadas o mal ejecutadas por un agente intermediario?
Viñeta Confianza, regulación y Open Finance: la automatización financiera promete eficiencia y personalización, pero sin marcos claros de responsabilidad, estándares de acceso seguro y educación financiera, el riesgo reputacional y operativo recae en el eslabón más débil.

La innovación avanza más rápido que los marcos de responsabilidad y cobertura. Los bancos buscan delimitar su exposición legal y operativa, mientras el mercado intenta definir las reglas de juego del agentic commerce y las finanzas asistidas por IA.  

¿Crees que es justo trasladar al cliente la responsabilidad por fallos o hackeos en herramientas de IA de terceros, o el sistema financiero y los seguros deben construir un modelo compartido de riesgo y protección?

text:
The three largest banks in the US now agree on one thing about AI agents. If you give one access to your account and something goes wrong, the loss is yours, even if the AI tool is the one that got hacked.

Citi updated its online user agreement this week, TechCrunch reported Wednesday. A Citi spokesperson said customers who give third party AI agents account access "are responsible for activities conducted through those agents."

JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America announced similar policies last month. PNC changed its terms Wednesday, and Citizens emailed customers a similar warning.

One thing the report does not settle: whether these terms cover business accounts. Read your own agreement before you assume they do not.

Here is why an owner should care. The pitch for AI bookkeeping and bill pay is simple: hand the tool your banking login and let it sort transactions and pay vendors.

That login was never meant to be shared, and the banks have now written down what that costs. Under Citi's terms, if the tool leaks your credentials, whatever happens next is on you. That is true even for a tool that only reads.

So the question is not which AI tool is smartest. It is how many tools are holding your keys.

This week, list every app that has your business banking login, AI or not. Disconnect anything you stopped using. For the rest, ask the vendor in writing whether it can move money and who pays if it gets breached.

How many apps do you think are connected to your business bank account right now?

text:
The next generation is about to inherit trillions. Most families are handing over a massive responsibility without ever teaching them how to carry it. 

That is a rather frightening thought when you consider how much wealth, responsibility and family history will change hands over the coming years.

Bank of America’s latest study of 355 family-office decision-makers found that 83% have identified a successor, yet only 27% have a trust distribution policy or written guiding principles.

So most families know who will take control. Far fewer have agreed on how that control should be exercised.

Who can access the capital? What should remain invested? How much risk is acceptable? Can family members sell their interests? Which decisions require agreement, and what happens when the family disagrees?

These questions may feel uncomfortable around the dinner table, but leaving them unanswered simply pushes the tension into the next generation.

The study also found that more complex family offices are considerably more likely to have formal investment policies, mission statements and independent governance. That makes perfect sense. As families grow across generations, marriages and jurisdictions, informal understandings become much harder to preserve.

For private client professionals, succession planning should therefore go well beyond identifying an heir and drafting the legal documents.

Help the family define the purpose of its wealth, create clear distribution principles and record how important decisions will be made. Bring future leaders into those conversations early enough to understand the responsibility they are inheriting, rather than introducing them when the signatures are required.

Choosing a successor protects continuity. Giving them clear rules may be what protects the family.

🔴 Bank of America — adopted this policy last month

Banks aren't just worried about security. They're worried about losing control of the customer relationship.
